issues.legal_issue: A remedial provision in a new rent-control law that clarifies or slightly modifies relief already available under the repealed law may govern pending eviction proceedings under the repealed law.
material_facts: The landlords brought eviction suits under the repealed rent-control law after tenants made structures contrary to conditions imposed on the landlords by the relevant authorities.
The tenants removed the offending structures while the suits were pending, leaving no further danger to the landlords’ leases.
The new rent-control law provided that eviction could be avoided if the tenant complied with the relevant condition or paid compensation as directed by the Controller.
The new provision was held to clarify and slightly modify relief that a court could already grant under the repealed law, by analogy with relief against forfeiture.
issues.conclusion: The new law’s provision for relief against eviction could be considered in the pending proceedings, and relief could be granted to tenants who remedied the breach.
issues.legal_principle: Under the first proviso to section 57(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, read harmoniously with section 57(2), the repealed law ordinarily governs pending proceedings, but clarifications or slight modifications in the new law may be applied; a radical departure may not. Karam Singh v. Sri Pratap Chand applied this approach. Section 14(11) of the 1958 Act was a clarification and slight modification of the relief that could have been granted under section 13(1)(k) of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952, by analogy with section 114-A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The court also relied on Uma Kumari v. Jaswant Rai Chopra in treating the eviction ground as analogous to forfeiture for breach of a lease condition.

rule.if: pending_ejectment_proceeding_under_prior_law and remedial_change_is_clarificatory and tenant_removed_offending_structure and breach_no_longer_endangers_lease

predicates.pending_ejectment_proceeding_under_prior: An eviction proceeding under an earlier rent-control law remained pending when a later rent-control law took effect.
predicates.remedial_change_is_clarificatory: The later law's provision for relief clarified or slightly modified relief that could already have been granted under the earlier law.
predicates.tenant_removed_offending_structure: The tenant removed the structure that had breached a condition imposed on the landlord.
predicates.breach_no_longer_endangers_lease: After the tenant remedied the breach, it no longer threatened the landlord's lease.
predicates.tenant_is_not_evicted: The tenant receives relief from eviction.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding under an earlier law is pending, the later law's clarifying remedial provision applies where the tenant removes the offending structure and the breach no longer endangers the landlord's lease, so the tenant is not evicted.

issues.legal_issue: When the statutory ground for eviction is established, eviction is required unless another provision provides relief.
material_facts: The eviction suits relied on tenants having used or dealt with the premises contrary to conditions imposed on the landlords by the relevant authorities.
The relevant lease conditions prohibited unauthorised structures, and the landlords relied on the tenants’ breaches as grounds for eviction.
The applicable rent-control provisions allowed relief against eviction where the tenant remedied the breach, and the tenants had removed the offending structures.
issues.conclusion: The eviction provisions were mandatory in substance when their requirements were met, but eviction was not required where a provision otherwise allowed relief.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 13(1) of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952, was framed imperatively. Although the proviso to section 14(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, used different language, there was no substantive difference: where its requirements were satisfied, eviction had to follow unless another provision of section 14, including sections 14(2), 14(10), or 14(11), provided otherwise.

predicates.statutory_ejectment_proceeding: A proceeding seeks eviction on a ground specified by the applicable rent-control law.
predicates.statutory_ejectment_ground_is_establishe: The facts satisfy the statutory requirements for the asserted ground of eviction.
predicates.no_applicable_relief_is_available: No applicable provision permits the tenant to avoid eviction despite the established ground.
predicates.eviction_is_required: The court or authority must order eviction.

issues.definition: In a statutory eviction proceeding, an established eviction ground requires eviction when no applicable provision affords the tenant relief.
